newsitem.title: USA: US 30-yr T-bond up full point after payroll report.
newsitem.headline: US 30-yr T-bond up full point after payroll report.

text.p: U.S. Treasury securities prices rallied early Friday after the government's June labor report showed fairly moderate growth in new jobs and wages and a rise in the unemployment rate to 5.0 percent in June from 4.8 percent in May.

The benchmark 30-year bond, which was up about 1/4 of a point before the employment report was released, briefly rose to 99-30/32, up 1-1/32, before trimming its gain. Its yield briefly fell to 6.63 percent, its lowest since February 21, when the bond yield closed at 6.64 percent.

The Labor Department reported that non-farm payrolls grew by 217,000 jobs in June after expanding by a revised 166,000 jobs in May. The government also reported that hourly wages rose to $12.22 an hour in June from $12.18 an hour in May.

"It's a fairly subdued report," said David Sloan, senior economist at I.D.E.A. "You have the weakest private sector payroll growth of the year. Average hourly earnings growth is nothing alarming and there's a rise in the unemployment rate as well. Overall I'd say this figure is pretty subdued."
Sloan said the payroll report argued against a Federal Reserve interest rate tightening in August.
"You'd have to see quite a pickup in payroll growth in the July figure to encourage the Fed to move in August," he said.
